drafted_from: tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts's row in tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts/tool-rows.json (its verify sample runs), do-work/check-against-their-rules-and-verdicts.mjs, do-work/check-a-branch.mjs and test/branch.test.mjs; the answer was observed by running check-a-branch.mjs on the sample's rows in an in-memory records door
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check the title 'A sparkle of zorblax' against my made-up-post branch of rules and tell me pass, fail or uncertain, with why." It reads your branch's rows from list:checks and says which rules the title breaks.

lists.label: Checks (the rules and branches you keep)
lists.holds: One node of your rule tree: a branch (a kind of thing you make) or a check (words, a pattern or a question that fails or holds a thing made), each naming the node it is part of.
alike: a style guide kept as a spreadsheet
a banned-words list in a notes app
the rule file of a writing linter

instructions: 1. Pour the four example rows into your own writing-rules list (see pour), or make list:checks from them: a branch made-up-base, a branch made-up-post that is part of it, and one word rule on each.

2. Say "Check this title against my made-up-post branch." The AI calls tools:run at @workshop-tools with tool tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts and { branch, units: [{ kind, text }] }. Give branch or rules, never both.

3. Read status (passed, failed, uncertain, unqualified or no-applicable-rule), results (each unit with its breaks, rule and the words found) and lines (the same in one readable block). A rule row with no test but a question comes back in questions: answer it and send the answers back in answers.

4. With no list, send rules directly (judge-words rows) and, to honour verdicts you already gave, verdict_rules and stands as tool:read-where-you-stand gives them: a stand of disagree on an exact line fails it first.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for your writing rules and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
